english.html: The brave are begotten of the brave and good; there is in bullocks, there is in horses, the virtue of their sires; nor do fierce eagles beget the unwarlike dove <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>.

notes.original: Horace au iij. li. des Carmes.
notes.gloss: Fortes creantur fortibus et bonis; / est in iuvencis, est in equis patrum / virtus, neque imbellem feroces / progenerant aquilae columbam.

english.html: So far as to see posterity bear now the sinews, now the scars, now whatever other marks of its ancestors and of its origin: witness the Roman Lepidi, of whom there were three of one house each having an eye covered with a little membrane; and Nicaeus of Byzantium, who was born black as a Moor, taking after his grandfather rather than his mother, who was fair and white, though begotten in adultery by an Ethiopian <sup class="mk" data-key="l">l</sup>. But the forces of nature and of race are not so great but that we sometimes see posterity degenerate and become unlike its progenitors: as from the handsome are born the ugly and deformed; from the robust and strong issue the impotent and weak; from the good and virtuous proceed the vicious and wicked <sup class="mk" data-key="m">m</sup>. Otherwise, if this did not sometimes happen so, it would be necessary, for the public good, to forbid by a general and inviolable law to the ugly, the feeble and the wicked marriage and carnal company with women, so that all might infallibly be born handsome, powerful and robust. Whereupon Alexander of Aphrodisias labours hard to sound out and show the cause why one often sees it happen that a stupid, gross and foolish man, nay a simpleton, will produce children who are clever, prudent, wise and discreet. And he concludes the reason to be that a dolt, in the venereal act, lets himself be so overcome and vanquished by the present pleasure that he then thinks of nothing else, having willingly plunged his mind and soul into the body; whence the seed, being drawn and taken from that body in which the mind is found, partakes greatly of the reasonable virtue, and makes the children who descend from it more prudent and intelligent than the father. As, on the contrary, with those who are ingenious, discreet or learned: because their mind incessantly works and busies itself elsewhere than with the pleasure of the flesh — even at the very instant of the act, in which it does not at all let itself be van

notes.original: Pline au liure vij. c. xij.
notes.gloss: Pliny: three Lepidi born with an eye covered by a membrane; Nicaeus the boxer of Byzantium, whose mother was born of adultery with an Ethiopian but was of ordinary colour, took after his Ethiopian grandfather. Pliny's marks are naevi et cicatrices, moles and scars; the print's nerfs ("sinews") is a slip for naeves.

notes.original: Plutarche au v. linre de placitis philoſophor. c. xij.
notes.gloss: The chapters of book V on why children resemble their parents, or others.

lines: Fortes creantur fortibus, & bonis,
Eſt in iuuencis, eſt in equis patrum
Virtus. nec imbellem feroces
Progenerant, aquilæ columbam {k}.
Iuſques à voir la poſterité, porter ores les nerfs, ores
les cicatrices, ores quelconques autres marques de ſes
anceſtres, & de ſon origine, teſmoins les Lepides Ro-
mains, deſquels y en eut trois d'vne maiſon, ayant cha-
cun l'œil couuert d'vne petite peau. Et Nice Bizantin,
qui naſquit noir comme vn more, rapportant pluttoſt
ſon ayeul, que ſa mere belle & blanche, engendrée tou-
tesfois, par adultere, d'vn Ethiopien {l}. Mais les ſorces de
la nature, ni des races, ne peuuent pas tant, que nous ne
voyons quelquefois la poſterité degenerer, & diſſembla
ble à ſes progeniteurs: cõme des beaux, naiſtre des laids
& difformes: des robuſtes & forts, iſſir des impuiſſans,
& foibles: des bons & vertueux, proceder des vicieux, &
meſchans {m}. Autrement, ſi par fois, cela n'aduenoit ain-
ſi faudroit pour le bien public defendre par loy gene-
rale & inuiolable, aux laids, debiles, & meſchans, le ma-
riage, & compagnie charnelle des femmes: afin que tous
infalliblement, naſquiſſent beaux, puiſſans, & robuſtes.
Sur quoy Alexandre Aphrodiſée, ſe trauaille fort à ſon-
der, & monſtrer la cauſe, pour laquelle on voit aduenir
ſouuent, qu'vn homme ſtupide, groſſier, & ſot, voire vn
nyés, produira des enfans accors, prudẽs; ſages, & diſcrets
Et conclud la raiſon eſtre, pour autant qu'vn badaut, en
l'acte venerien, ſe laiſſe tellement ſurmonter, & vaincre
à la volupté preſente, qu'il ne penſe lors à autre choſe:
ayant volontairement plongé l'eſprit, & l'ame dans le
corps, dont la ſemence eſt puiſée & tirée de ce corps
parmy lequel l'eſprit ſe trouue, participe grandement
de la vertu raiſonnable: & fait que les enfans, qui en
deſcendent, ſont plus prudens, & ſpirituels que le pere.
Comme au contraire, ceux qui ſont ingenieux, diſcrets,
ou ſçauans, par ce que leur eſprit inceſſammẽt trauaille,
& ſ'occupe ailleurs qu'au plaiſir de la chair: voire meſ-
mes ſur l'inſtãt de l'acte, auquel du tout ne ſe laiſſe vain
Horace au
iij. li. des Car-
mes.
Pline au li-
ure vij. c. xij.

au v. linre de

uncertain.note: 'inceſſammẽt' — the mark over the e is a short slightly tilted bar, read as nasal tilde (= incessamment), not an acute accent

uncertain.note: 'l'inſtãt' — straight bar over the a read as nasal tilde (= instant); last body line, the word 'vain' runs on to the next page

numeral read as 'iij' (three dots, third minim descends as j) at 9x; at reading size it can look like 'ij'. Horace's Carmina book for this stanza is in fact IV, so the print may be in error, but 'iij' is what is set

a very faint blind/offset impression of three or four short marks sits below the last body line at the left, where a signature would fall; it is illegible even at 6x with contrast stretched and folio 15 would not normally be signed, so signature is recorded as null

uncertain.text: nyés, produira des enfans accors, prudẽs; ſages, & diſcrets
uncertain.note: 'prudẽs' with a straight bar over the e read as nasal tilde. The mark after it is printed as two pieces, a dot over a comma wedge, read as a semicolon (reader A read a comma). The line ends after 'diſcrets' with no punctuation although a new sentence follows (sic).

uncertain.text: tesfois, par adultere, d'vn Ethiopien {l}. Mais les ſorces de
uncertain.note: 'tesfois' has a round short s before the crossbarred f. 'ſorces': at 8x the initial sort has a hooked top and a left nub only, no crossbar to the right, unlike the f of 'forts' four lines below: a long ſ set for f, sic for 'forces' (both readers).
the note's key letter is printed as an italic CAPITAL K followed by a period ('K. Horace au'); the body marker is a raised lowercase k. Recorded as key k.

the third letter of the word after 'v.' prints with its stems joined at the top (italic n), so 'linre': a turned or wrong sort for 'liure' (reader A read 'liure'). Pointer: pages/full/p015.jpg x~2355-2420, y~1928-1985.
at 6x two dots are visible, the second over the letter before the final s: 'placitis' (De placitis philosophorum), not 'placitus'.
